name: HOG Anomaly Detection
description: Analyzes gradient orientation distributions using Histogram of Oriented Gradients. AI images exhibit more uniform gradient orientations than natural scenes.
algorithm: Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) + Entropy Analysis
mechanism: Computes gradient magnitudes and orientations, bins them into 9 bins. Higher entropy indicates more uniform distribution typical of AI.
parameters: Bins: 9, Orientation: unsigned [0,PI], Metric: normalized entropy
useCase: Detecting uniform gradient orientations in AI-generated content

references.title: Dalal, N. & Triggs, B. (2005). Histograms of Oriented Gradients for Human Detection. CVPR.
Felzenszwalb, P.F. et al. (2010). Object Detection with Part-Based Models. IEEE TPAMI.
Lyu, S. & Farid, H. (2005). How Realistic is Photorealistic? IEEE TSP.

strengths:
• Captures local shape and gradient structure effectively
• Well-proven in computer vision since 2005
• Detects structural inconsistencies in AI-generated content
• Multi-scale orientation analysis
• Robust to illumination changes due to gradient normalization
limitations:
• Computationally intensive for dense extraction
• Cell and block size parameters affect sensitivity
• Textured regions may produce noisy descriptors
• Limited effectiveness on smooth, featureless regions
• AI models increasingly generate realistic gradient structures
